hypotheses.name: Depth-migrating magnetotelluric edge vector
layers: Competition MT resistivity/depth slices named in the prior feature manifest: 500 m, 1 km, 2 km, 4 km, 6 km, and 10 km
hypotheses.physical_signature: Track the lateral displacement vector of coherent conductivity-gradient ridges between consecutive depth slices; require monotonic migration consistent with a dipping plane, then project the inferred plane to the surface. Do not use a single shallow/deep gradient magnitude as the score.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: A buried dipping conduit or alteration zone can be laterally displaced from its surface trace. Cross-depth migration could therefore prioritize a blind structure not present in a surface-fault catalogue.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Depth-dependent inversion smoothing or a basin-margin conductor; require coherent displacement across adjacent depth slices and sensitivity to inversion resolution before interpreting it as a fault.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The previous H86B lane uses shallow/deep MT gradients and a vertical contrast; the proposed transform is the vector/plane geometry rather than another scalar edge. However, the exact depth-migrating MT idea was already written as H86E-MTDA in research/H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md and was not tested here.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: Not novel relative to repository text: H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md already describes this depth-migration/up-dip projection proposal. It is re-ranked here, not claimed as a new method or globally unique approach.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Highest qualitative potential among the locally specified shortlist for blind-fault coverage; this is a scientific prior, not a numerical score estimate.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: depth registration, coherence tracking, geometric projection, and fold-safe ablations.
hypotheses.data_availability: Requires the official competition training_features.tif MT bands and the template's cached feature stack. An earlier H86B review described the six slices as locally verified in that earlier session; the owner-mirror feature raster is hash-pinned in research/upstream/data_manifest.json but absent from this checkout, and no official organizer download was authenticated here. Not currently viable to validate under the cache-reuse rule.

hypotheses.name: Paired potential-field ridge dislocation with transverse gravity step
layers: Competition RTP/TMI, upward-continued TMI, complete Bouguer gravity, and basement-depth bands
hypotheses.physical_signature: Extract phase-symmetry ridge segments at more than one scale; graph-match conjugate terminations with consistent strike across a lateral offset; score only the intervening corridor when a transverse gravity-gradient step corroborates it.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: A concealed cross-fault can displace an older magnetic marker contact. Scoring the termination/offset corridor rather than the contact itself may reveal the cross-fault away from mapped surface traces.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Caldera-ring geometry, intrusive contacts, and survey-mosaic seams; require conjugate geometry across scales and independent gravity support, and test acquisition-axis concentration.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The paired-endpoint and transverse-bridge formulation adds multi-scale matching and corroboration to earlier potential-field edge/contact features. A related displaced-contact concept already appears as a prior candidate in research/REVIEW.md, so this is a refinement, not a wholly new repository idea.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: Not wholly novel relative to repository text: research/REVIEW.md already proposes paired magnetic-contact endpoints with gravity corroboration. No global sibling-repository novelty audit is complete.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Medium-high qualitative potential; it targets a structural discontinuity rather than another continuous contact, but its expected value is uncertain.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: ridge graph construction, endpoint pairing, offset constraints, and fold-stable controls.
hypotheses.data_availability: Uses competition geophysics/topography channels only, if the official feature stack is restored. No new external raster is required. The shared cached stack is absent here, so it is not currently viable to validate under the prompt.

hypotheses.name: Relief-normalized LiDAR scarplet chains with shoreline and drainage rejection
layers: USGS 3DEP-derived one-metre LiDAR scarp features, elevation, and slope
hypotheses.physical_signature: Detect multi-azimuth scarplet chains at piedmont scale after normalizing by local relief; reject contour-parallel benches and dendritic channel edges using tangent-to-contour and drainage alignment tests.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: Low-slip or intrabasin fault scarps can be weak in a 100 m DEM but persist as aligned metre-scale breaks across an alluvial piedmont where no catalogue trace is mapped.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Pluvial shoreline benches, fan-channel incision, and roads; explicitly suppress contour-parallel and drainage-aligned responses and verify persistence across independent LiDAR-derived channels.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Contour-orthogonality and drainage rejection sharpen a LiDAR scarplet-chain idea already proposed as H86C-TDPL in research/H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md. H86B also used LiDAR scarplet features; the dedicated rejection transform is not documented as a completed standalone ablation in the reviewed current evidence.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: Not new at the hypothesis level: H86C-TDPL was previously proposed in research/H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md. Only the explicit shoreline/drainage rejection ablation may be a refinement; no global novelty claim is supported.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Moderate qualitative potential; high native-resolution surface detail is attractive, but the competition holdout is catalogue-based and may not represent blind intrabasin targets.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Moderate: the owner-mirror product is already described in the manifest, but multi-scale orientation and mimic rejection need careful testing.
hypotheses.data_availability: The local manifest describes a hash-pinned owner-derived LiDAR product sourced from USGS 3DEP; the raster itself is absent from this checkout, and its official tile-level provenance/coverage has not been independently rechecked here. The named official source is available for manual review but is outside the sandbox's allowed outbound hosts.

hypotheses.name: Relocated microseismic planes with uncertainty-aware up-dip projection
layers: Raw USGS ComCat events with moment tensors and location uncertainty; not the supplied broad earthquake-density bands
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fit spatially coherent three-dimensional hypocentre planes with uncertainty weighting, test nodal-plane orientation where available, and project the accepted plane up-dip to its surface intersection.
hypotheses.missing_fault_mechanism: A seismogenic blind fault may produce a planar hypocentre fabric before a surface trace is mapped; explicit depth geometry can localize a concealed structure better than broad smoothed seismic-density bands.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Quarry blasts, fluid-injection swarms, and migrating earthquake sequences; use event-type, depth, uncertainty, and temporal-coherence filters.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The uncertainty-aware plane fit and up-dip projection elaborate an earlier H86F-RLSL proposal in research/H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md; this is not a new hypothesis within the repository. It differs from broad seismic-density and event-count features, but any specific source-catalogue overlap still requires registry review.
hypotheses.repository_novelty: Previously proposed in research/H86B_GFCO_REVIEW.md as H86F-RLSL. Not novel at the repository proposal level; not tested in this review and no global sibling comparison is complete.
hypotheses.expected_dti_potential: Potentially high but highly uncertain; sparse event coverage may leave much of the footprint uninformative.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High, plus a separate data-ingestion and provenance audit.
hypotheses.data_availability: Specific free official source: USGS ComCat FDSN event API. It is outside the sandbox outbound allowlist and no event file is present; a previous repository note records external-USGS egress failure. Not viable here until an official-source mirror is legally and hash-verifiably obtained.
